name: Agent must/must-not generate rules + scan IDs for Python services
short_definition: Binding agent codegen policy for Python in the engineer stack: what agents must always emit (uv+src layout, FastAPI lifespan, Pydantic v2, basedpyright, PyJWT with algorithms, timeouts, health probes, OpenAPI contracts) and must never emit (Poetry/Black/mypy greenfield defaults, python-jose, sync requests in async routes, BackgroundTasks for money, dual migrations, leaked secrets). Pairs machine-checkable scan IDs with positive/negative signals for engineer-scan and code review. As of 2026-07-13, synthesizes all researched py-* leaf items into one agent-facing rule surface.
scope_in: Must-generate / must-not-generate checklists for agents scaffolding or editing Python services
Scan ID catalog (PY-*) for enforcement and review rubrics
Positive and negative code signals mapped to clusters (tooling, language, web, data, workers, quality)
Greenfield template completeness bar (files, CI, settings, auth, DB, tests)
How agent policy differs from human brownfield exception process
Cross-language boundary rules agents must respect (TS BFF owns cookies; Python verifies Bearer; Rust for measured hot paths)
scope_out: Full narrative tutorials (live in leaf research + future references/python.md)
One-off ops scripts outside services/packages layout

defaults.agent_posture: Python is a peer service language for AI, workers, OpenAPI APIs — never the UI shell; Next/TS remains product boundary
defaults.scaffold_stack: CPython 3.13 + uv + ruff + basedpyright + pytest + FastAPI + Pydantic v2 + SQLAlchemy 2 async + uvicorn
always_emit_patterns: AppError + exception handlers; no stack traces to clients
response_model / separate In/Out models; extra='forbid' on public inputs
defaults.policy_severity: hard-fail on must_not_generate in greenfield; warn+ticket for brownfield migration

use_when: Agent generates or refactors any Python service under services/ or packages/
Writing scan rules, evals, or skill module bullets for Python
Greenfield monorepo adding first Python package
do_not_use_when: Pure TS/Next feature with no Python process
Legacy codebase under explicit migration plan that temporarily violates a rule with documented exception
Research notebooks or one-off analysis scripts not shipping as product services
alternatives: typescript.md agent norms for Server Actions/Zod
Leaf py-* research for domain depth beyond this synthesis

do: Emit uv-only packaging: pyproject + uv.lock + .python-version; never Poetry greenfield
Use FastAPI lifespan (not on_event) for pools and clients
Validate all external input with Pydantic v2 model_validate; ConfigDict not class Config
Annotate public APIs; PEP 695 / X|None / list[str]; CI basedpyright
Verify JWT with explicit algorithms; AuthN Depends + AuthZ ownership checks
Time-box all external I/O; structured concurrency (TaskGroup/anyio) for multi-child work
Tier jobs: BackgroundTasks only best-effort; Taskiq for durable async; Temporal for multi-step
One migration owner per DB; RLS with CREATE TABLE when Supabase owns schema
Map domain errors at edge; log with request_id; return safe client messages
Include ruff format+check, basedpyright, pytest unit, uv audit in CI
dont: Don't scaffold black/isort/flake8/mypy as greenfield defaults
Don't use python-jose, jwt.decode without algorithms, or verify_signature=False
Don't use requests or time.sleep inside async routes
Don't create_task without a supervisor for request-scoped work
Don't use BackgroundTasks for payments, compliance, or must-not-lose work
Don't dual-migrate the same tables with Alembic and Supabase
Don't return ORM objects as JSON; don't session.query in new code
Don't hardcode secrets or log SecretStr/settings dumps

code_skeleton:
# Agent greenfield checklist (emit all of these or document exception)

# pyproject.toml essentials
# [project] name, requires-python = ">=3.13", dependencies = [...]
# [dependency-groups] dev = ["ruff", "basedpyright", "pytest", "pytest-asyncio", "httpx"]
# [tool.ruff] target-version = "py313"
# [tool.basedpyright] typeCheckingMode = "recommended", pythonVersion = "3.13"
# [tool.pytest.ini_options] asyncio_mode = "auto", markers = ["unit", "integration"]

# src/app/main.py shape
from contextlib import asynccontextmanager
from typing import Annotated, AsyncIterator
from fastapi import Depends, FastAPI
from pydantic import BaseModel, ConfigDict, Field

class ItemIn(BaseModel):
    model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid")
    name: str = Field(min_length=1, max_length=200)

@asynccontextmanager
async def lifespan(app: FastAPI) -> AsyncIterator[None]:
    # create engine, httpx.AsyncClient, redis; yield; aclose/dispose
    yield

app = FastAPI(lifespan=lifespan)

# MUST: health, settings via Depends, JWT algorithms explicit, thin routers
failure_modes: Agent scaffolds Poetry + Black + mypy → fights monorepo uv/ruff policy and CI
Agent copies FastAPI tutorials with on_event and global engine at import → flaky tests, leaked pools
Agent uses BackgroundTasks for billing/webhooks → silent data loss on crash
Agent omits algorithms= on jwt.decode → algorithm confusion / none alg attacks
Agent uses Supabase pooler URL without asyncpg prepared-statement mitigations → intermittent 500s
Agent dual-writes schema via create_all + manual SQL → prod drift
Agent emits untyped public handlers → basedpyright fails or is skipped
Agent logs full settings/tokens → secret sprawl in log sinks
anti_patterns: Generating 'compatible with everything' stacks (Poetry AND uv, Black AND ruff)
Silent # type: ignore / # noqa without rule codes
Tutorial-default CORS * and reload in prod manifests
Treating Python as the cookie session authority instead of verifying Bearer from Next/Supabase
Msgspec or Celery as silent defaults without tier decision

ts_boundary: Agents must keep cookie SSR auth, Server Actions, and UI in Next/TS. Python agents generate Bearer/JWT verification and OpenAPI servers that TS consumes via codegen — never dual session systems. Mirror typescript.md: Zod at TS boundary ↔ Pydantic at Python boundary.
rust_boundary: Agents must not rewrite working FastAPI into Axum without measured need. When generating hot-path services, follow rust.md (no unwrap in handlers, timeouts). Prefer Python for AI glue/RAG/iteration; Rust for p99/cpu-bound gateways.
supabase_boundary: Agents: product schema + RLS → supabase/migrations. Python service-role SQLAlchemy for server transactions with explicit authz in code. Never put SERVICE_ROLE in client-facing handlers or NEXT_PUBLIC_*.
